what: NVIDIA designs graphics processors (GPUs) and complete computing systems that have become the main engine for training and running AI models. It has no factories; TSMC makes its chips.
customers: Cloud giants such as Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Meta, AI labs, governments, and, on a smaller scale, gamers, designers and carmakers.
money: Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, full servers and networking
chips for design, simulation and self-driving cars
moat: The CUDA software ecosystem that millions of developers build on, leading chip design, networking (NVLink, InfiniBand) and selling whole systems rather than single chips.
rivals: In-house chips from Google, Amazon and Microsoft
risks: Revenue depends on the spending of a few cloud customers; an AI slowdown would hit fast
US export limits on sales to China
Customers designing their own chips, and competition from AMD
opportunities: Revenue grew about 65% last year and about 100% a year over three years
Operating margin of 60% and return on invested capital of 66%
Analysts see about 62% upside, with data centre demand still exceeding supply
watch: Data centre revenue growth and whether supply constraints ease.
